report.title: Overview
paragraphs: This projection runs 120 months (10 years) from 2026-08. You start with 50 does and 2 bucks — 61 head on the ground in month 1.
The project needs ₹20.19 lakh in total: ₹17.16 lakh from the bank and ₹3.03 lakh from your own pocket, with ₹0 assumed up-front subsidy.

report.title: Herd trajectory
paragraphs: The herd grows from 61 head in month 1 to a peak of 135 in month 90 (year 8), ending at 126 head (48 breeding does and 3 bucks).
Over the 10 years the farm produces 1018 kids, loses 232 animals to mortality, sells 556 for meat and disposes of 167 as culls.

Expect multiples at kidding: this breed twins in about 35-40% of kiddings and triplets run 5-13%, so the average mature litter is ~1.60 kids. First-time does (parity 1) run lighter — about 1.36 on average, mostly singles — so a maiden crop of singles is normal, not a problem.

report.title: Where the money comes from
paragraphs: Total revenue over 10 years is ₹88.60 lakh, largest source first: meat sales ₹67.77 lakh (76.5%), cull sales ₹15.26 lakh (17.2%), manure ₹5.57 lakh (6.3%) and surplus milk ₹0 (0.0%).
Bakrid pricing (+35% on the base rate) applies in months 10, 22, 33, 45, 57, 68, 80, 91, 103, 115; 108 head sell inside them.

report.title: Where the money goes
paragraphs: Operating costs total ₹76.12 lakh over 10 years, largest first: feed ₹36.45 lakh (47.9%), labour ₹21.61 lakh (28.4%), vet ₹7.15 lakh (9.4%), insurance ₹4.38 lakh (5.8%), selling ₹3.44 lakh (4.5%), overheads ₹3.09 lakh (4.1%) and stock purchases ₹0 (0.0%).
Buying breeding stock cost ₹2.13 lakh in cash; it is capitalized and depreciated over 60 months rather than expensed, so EBITDA above excludes it.

Growing green fodder needs about 3.06 acre(s) on average; your cultivated area falls short in 93 month(s). This is a physical and financial shortfall: 29,184 kg as-fed is bought at the configured market price, while on-farm supply is costed separately.
Water demand runs about 754 litres/day on average, peaking near 824 litres/day — a lactating doe needs 10-15 L/day in the Deccan summer, so plan storage and supply for the peak, not the average.

report.title: Bottom line
paragraphs: At these assumptions the project is NOT VIABLE. Over 10 years it earns ₹88.60 lakh against ₹76.12 lakh of operating costs — an operating surplus (EBITDA) of ₹12.48 lakh.

Watch out: the NPV is negative; the benefit-cost ratio is below 1.0; a unique IRR is not established (assessment: indeterminate); use NPV and MIRR; the weakest debt year has a DSCR below 1.0; the funded working-capital reserve becomes negative and additional liquidity is needed.

report.title: Risks
paragraphs: Run with Monte Carlo and sensitivity enabled to see how robust these results are to price swings, disease and poor breeding years.
Ordinary IRR uniqueness is unproven in this solver domain; use NPV and MIRR.
Embedded future festival dates are projections requiring local confirmation; moon sighting can change the sale month near a month boundary. 2039 has both January and December occurrences.

explanation.title: Accounting profit
explanation.explanation: Cumulative profit after depreciation, disposed breeding-stock carrying costs, interest and tax is -₹6.54 lakh. This accrual profit excludes terminal asset recovery and differs from cash flow because depreciation and disposal book costs are non-cash while principal repayment is not an expense.

explanation.title: Liquidity low point
explanation.explanation: The operating cash reserve reaches its low point of -₹3.27 lakh in month 21 (year 2). The plan therefore needs at least another ₹3.27 lakh beyond the funded working-capital reserve to avoid a cash shortfall.

explanation.title: Operating margin
explanation.explanation: EBITDA is -18.0% of operating revenue over the projection. This isolates farm operations before depreciation, financing and tax.

explanation.title: Payback period
explanation.explanation: Cumulative cash flow never covers your ₹3.01 lakh equity within the 24-month horizon.

explanation.explanation: The break-even meat price was not computed for this run. Re-run with the break-even search enabled to see how far the price can fall.

report.title: Overview
paragraphs: This projection runs 24 months (2 years) from 2026-08. You start with 50 does and 2 bucks — 61 head on the ground in month 1.
The project needs ₹20.07 lakh in total: ₹17.06 lakh from the bank and ₹3.01 lakh from your own pocket, with ₹0 assumed up-front subsidy.

report.title: Herd trajectory
paragraphs: The herd grows from 61 head in month 1 to a peak of 133 in month 21 (year 2), ending at 127 head (49 breeding does and 3 bucks).
Over the 2 years the farm produces 212 kids, loses 45 animals to mortality, sells 78 for meat and disposes of 15 as culls.

Expect multiples at kidding: this breed twins in about 35-40% of kiddings and triplets run 5-13%, so the average mature litter is ~1.60 kids. First-time does (parity 1) run lighter — about 1.36 on average, mostly singles — so a maiden crop of singles is normal, not a problem.

report.title: Where the money comes from
paragraphs: Total revenue over 2 years is ₹10.17 lakh, largest source first: meat sales ₹8.07 lakh (79.3%), cull sales ₹1.15 lakh (11.3%), manure ₹95,502 (9.4%) and surplus milk ₹0 (0.0%).
Bakrid pricing (+35% on the base rate) applies in months 10, 22; 15 head sell inside them.

report.title: Where the money goes
paragraphs: Operating costs total ₹12.00 lakh over 2 years, largest first: feed ₹5.83 lakh (48.6%), labour ₹3.52 lakh (29.3%), vet ₹1.08 lakh (9.0%), insurance ₹68,771 (5.7%), overheads ₹50,318 (4.2%), selling ₹37,620 (3.1%) and stock purchases ₹0 (0.0%).
Buying breeding stock cost ₹19,784 in cash; it is capitalized and depreciated over 60 months rather than expensed, so EBITDA above excludes it.

Growing green fodder needs about 2.86 acre(s) on average; your cultivated area falls short in 14 month(s). This is a physical and financial shortfall: 5,052 kg as-fed is bought at the configured market price, while on-farm supply is costed separately.
Water demand runs about 707 litres/day on average, peaking near 819 litres/day — a lactating doe needs 10-15 L/day in the Deccan summer, so plan storage and supply for the peak, not the average.

report.title: Bottom line
paragraphs: At these assumptions the project is NOT VIABLE. Over 2 years it earns ₹10.17 lakh against ₹12.00 lakh of operating costs — an operating surplus (EBITDA) of -₹1.83 lakh.

Watch out: the NPV is negative; the benefit-cost ratio is below 1.0; a unique IRR is not established (assessment: indeterminate); use NPV and MIRR; the weakest debt year has a DSCR below 1.0; the equity is never paid back inside the horizon; the funded working-capital reserve becomes negative and additional liquidity is needed.

report.title: Risks
paragraphs: Across 10 correlated Monte Carlo runs (varying prices, feed, fodder yield, operating cost, mortality and reproduction, plus monthly adverse events and year-to-year price swings within each run), the NPV averages -₹4.59 lakh with a 90% range of -₹5.51 lakh to -₹3.65 lakh. The project loses money in 100.0% of runs and runs short of operating cash in 100.0%. Every risk path also draws disease events/drought events/market-crash events events, so this distribution sits below the headline (no-disaster) figures — compare runs against each other, not against the deterministic base case.

These figures carry sampling noise at 10 runs: the 5th-percentile NPV is -₹5.51 lakh with a bootstrap 95% interval of -₹5.63 lakh to -₹4.89 lakh, and the loss probability of 100.0% has a standard error of 0.0%. More runs narrow both.
The assumptions that move NPV the most: meat price (+20.0% moves NPV by ₹1.92 lakh), litter size (-20.0% moves NPV by -₹1.35 lakh), feed prices (-20.0% moves NPV by ₹1.13 lakh).
Ordinary IRR uniqueness is unproven in this solver domain; use NPV and MIRR.
Embedded future festival dates are projections requiring local confirmation; moon sighting can change the sale month near a month boundary. 2039 has both January and December occurrences.
